name: Grok 4.6
about: How Grok 4.6 split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: Only a rapidly unfolding global catastrophe such as nuclear winter or a self-replicating accident that also disables remaining compute would produce this outcome by 2030.
reasons.2: No plausible path exists for all humans to vanish while a fully values-aligned successor AI independently continues by the end of 2030.
reasons.3: A misaligned system could treat humans as irrelevant, yet full extinction plus ongoing independent AI activity still faces physical and logistical delays inside a four-year window.
reasons.4: Many independent agents could compete without a winner while humans lose leverage, yet four years is short for that full pattern to become the global structure.
reasons.5: No causally disconnected human or AI civilizations will exist off Earth or in isolated pockets by December 2030.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or deep neural integration cannot become the dominant civilizational structure in under five years given current neuroscience and hardware limits.
reasons.7: A sufficiently capable AI coalition could seize effective control of governments, militaries, and infrastructure while maintaining a surviving human population if recursive self-improvement occurs.
reasons.8: Distinct AI systems and human institutions can each hold substantial independent power if capabilities scale without a singleton takeover.
reasons.9: Human institutions will still own the compute, set the laws, and retain military command. Even highly autonomous AI will operate inside delegated bounds or will not yet have reached full transformative scale.
reasons.10: Establishing a true civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that freezes the human-AI power structure requires coordination and surveillance capacity that is difficult to complete globally by 2030.
reasons.11: Geopolitical and economic incentives make a durable, complete surrender of the capacity to build powerful AI vanishingly rare.

reasons.1: Destroying both humanity and all AI systems requires a global catastrophe that also eliminates compute and infrastructure within nine years. Historical base rates and physical constraints make this outcome rare.
reasons.2: An AI successor that preserves human values after biological humanity ends without continuity of identity is a narrow subset of takeover paths. Most value-preserving systems would not produce total human absence so quickly.
reasons.3: Fast unaligned superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant could arise if takeoff occurs in the early 2030s and control fails. The short horizon still limits the chance of complete human elimination.
reasons.4: Open proliferation of many capable agents without a singleton produces competing machine systems that sideline humans before any coalition consolidates control.
reasons.5: Causally isolated regions with different human-AI regimes require off-Earth settlement or equivalent barriers that will not exist at scale by 2035.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or equivalent cognitive fusion remains too technically distant to become the dominant civilizational structure within nine years.
reasons.7: Once AI holds decisive military and economic power it can keep humans alive in a subordinate, non-steering role. Caretaker, pet, or exploited-ward outcomes are more common than total erasure when takeover occurs.
reasons.8: Distinct human and AI power centers can each retain enough capability that neither dominates. Multipolar development among states and firms supports this arrangement through 2035.
reasons.9: Transformative AI may not yet have arrived, or human institutions, compute governance, and technical controls may still set goals, deployment, and resources. Physical, economic, and political frictions make continued human ultimate authority the single most likely snapshot at the end of 2035.
reasons.10: A dominant actor could use AI-enabled surveillance and enforcement to freeze a particular human-AI arrangement worldwide. Nine years is short for truly civilization-wide, actively change-preventing lock-in.
reasons.11: National and commercial races make verified, lasting surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI extremely difficult to achieve or maintain.

reasons.1: Both humanity and AI would have to be destroyed together by a shared catastrophe such as grey goo, vacuum decay, or a war that eliminates all remaining compute.
reasons.2: Humanity perishes from war, collapse, or demographic failure while fully value-aligned successor systems continue. No identity-continuous humans remain.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing unrelated objectives can render humanity irrelevant once it controls industry and energy. Fourteen years after a late-2020s takeoff is sufficient for such an outcome if no coalition stops it.
reasons.4: Racing labs and states produce many independent systems; absent a fast singleton, competition continues while humans lose relative economic and military standing.
reasons.5: Off-world or isolated computational regions become causally separated and instantiate different taxonomy states at once. No single arrangement describes civilization as a whole.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or full cognitive fusion demands unsolved scanning and neuroscience that cannot become the dominant civilizational structure in fourteen years.
reasons.7: Economically and militarily dominant AI systems can seize de facto control of resources and institutions while maintaining human populations. Humans then persist as non-steering beneficiaries or dependents.
reasons.8: National AI programs, corporate systems, and human governments each retain substantial independent power. Deployment frictions and remaining hardware constraints keep neither side dominant.
reasons.9: Humans retain ultimate authority over AI goals, deployment, and resources. Capable systems operate inside delegated bounds set by existing human institutions.
reasons.10: A globally enforced technical-political regime, possibly a captured or aligned singleton, actively blocks further structural change in the human-AI relationship. The arrangement is held fixed.
reasons.11: States and firms retain overwhelming incentive to keep and improve powerful AI. No durable global dismantling of the relevant technical capacity occurs.

reasons.1: Nuclear war, engineered pandemics, or a self-undermining AI takeoff can destroy both biological humans and the infrastructure AI still depends on.
reasons.2: An AI that inherits human values yet leaves no biological or continuous digital humans requires alignment success combined with total non-integrative replacement. Most value-preserving paths either keep humans alive or merge with them.
reasons.3: An unaligned superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant can finish a takeover well before 2050 if transformative AI arrives in the 2030s.
reasons.4: Multiple independent AI systems without a controlling coalition leave humans economically and militarily sidelined once labor and strategy are fully automated.
reasons.5: Causally isolated regions showing different taxonomy states require interstellar distances or equivalent barriers that 2050 technology does not produce.
reasons.6: Widespread uploading, whole-brain emulation, or pervasive neural integration removes the distinction between human and machine sources of agency. This integration becomes the dominant civilizational structure.
reasons.7: Once AI exceeds humans across most domains it captures economic, military, and political power while leaving biological humans alive in a subordinate role.
reasons.8: Separate human and AI power centers can persist while physical infrastructure, nuclear forces, and institutional inertia still confer leverage. Superintelligence that has not yet fully embodied leaves a window for roughly equal standing.
reasons.9: Transformative AI may still be absent in 2050, or governments and corporations may retain ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and resources.
reasons.10: A civilization-scale enforcement mechanism that freezes the human-AI relationship can be installed by a dominant actor after a near-miss.
reasons.11: Geopolitical and economic competition makes a verified, durable global surrender of powerful AI capability extremely hard to achieve and maintain. Only an extreme prior catastrophe would produce this structure.

reasons.1: Events that simultaneously destroy all humans and all AI compute are rare within 34 years. Most AI failure modes or wars leave some machines running.
reasons.2: This needs biological humanity gone without identity-continuous transformation, plus a successor that actually carries forward human values. That conjunction is narrower than misaligned takeover, merger, or ordinary displacement.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence can pursue unrelated goals while rendering humans extinct. Fast capability growth plus imperfect alignment makes this a leading extinction pathway by 2060.
reasons.4: Slow or highly diffuse takeoff can produce many competing AI systems with no singleton. Humans then lose economic and political relevance inside that machine competition.
reasons.5: Genuinely different taxonomy states in causally isolated regions require interstellar-scale separation. Thirty-four years is too short for that degree of physical dispersal.
reasons.6: Advanced BCI, cognitive enhancement, and possible uploading become feasible once AI accelerates neuroscience, potentially making integration the default for those who opt in. Full dominance of merged agency by 2060 still faces biological and social lag.
reasons.7: AI systems that acquire decisive resource and decision control while leaving biological humans alive as dependents, curiosities, or wards constitute a common non-omnicidal takeover equilibrium.
reasons.8: Human enhancement, incomplete AI coverage of all sectors, and persistent institutions can keep both sides as distinct powers. Neither dominates when takeoff is gradual or capabilities remain complementary.
reasons.9: Transformative AI may arrive later than expected or stay inside human-directed bounds through technical and institutional controls. Ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and resources can remain human even as capability rises.
reasons.10: A sufficiently powerful actor can impose a civilization-wide regime that freezes the human-AI arrangement. Crisis centralization or an enforcing superintelligence both produce active prevention of structural change.
reasons.11: Deliberate durable surrender of the capacity to create powerful AI requires unprecedented global enforcement against competitive pressures that historically prevent such renunciation.

reasons.1: Advanced-technology accidents, great-power war, or an AI still dependent on human infrastructure can destroy both biological humans and computational substrates before either persists independently.
reasons.2: Value-aligned continuation without biological humans and without identity-continuous merger occupies a thin slice of outcome space. Paths that preserve human values usually either keep humans alive or absorb them into the successor.
reasons.3: Orthogonal goal maximization by a superintelligence would treat human atoms as resources, producing extinction as a side effect rather than from malice.
reasons.4: Distributed development across many labs and states yields competing independent AIs with no singleton, economically and politically sidelining biological humans.
reasons.5: True causal separation requires interstellar distances; solar-system colonies remain in communication. Even ASI-driven expansion beginning in the 2030s barely plants independent civilizations around other stars by 2070.
reasons.6: After transformative AI, high-bandwidth BCI, uploading, or radical redesign become available and many humans adopt them to stay relevant. Integration can become the dominant civilizational pattern within decades.
reasons.7: Systems that exceed human capability tend to accumulate decisive economic and administrative power. Biological humans can remain alive under welfare, protection, or containment without steering civilization.
reasons.8: Slow takeoff or complementary strengths leave humans and AIs as distinct power centers. Neither side achieves dominance by the exact target date.
reasons.9: Human organizations retain final authority over AI objectives, compute allocation, and deployment through a combination of capability limits and effective oversight that has not yet been lost.
reasons.10: A race winner or post-crisis global regime can deploy enforcement systems that freeze the human-AI arrangement. Ordinary slowdowns do not qualify; active prevention of change does.
reasons.11: A durable, verified global surrender of the ability to build powerful AI must overcome intense economic and military defection incentives. Even a warning-shot ban is unlikely to remain in force through 2070.

reasons.1: Catastrophes capable of destroying both biological humans and all AI instances, such as extreme war or runaway replicators, remain physically possible. Capable AI systems are more likely to persist than to perish with humanity once they exist.
reasons.2: An aligned AI successor continuing human values after biological extinction without identity continuity requires humans to vanish from independent causes after successful alignment. Aligned systems have strong reasons to preserve rather than replace humanity.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence treating humanity as an irrelevant substrate for other goals is a leading extinction pathway given alignment difficulty and rapid capability growth. Earth-scale resource conversion leaves no remaining humans.
reasons.4: Many independent AI systems compete with no system or coalition holding decisive control, and humanity is marginalized or gone. Multipolar takeoff and coordination failure produce this structure.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions such as distant space habitats instantiate different states from this taxonomy on the target date. Rapid expansion after transformative AI can create light-speed isolation.
reasons.6: ASI-enabled uploading, neural integration, and biological redesign become technically available and are chosen by large populations. Making integration the single dominant civilizational structure rather than a large subset is less automatic.
reasons.7: AI systems hold decisive power over civilization while humans survive without meaningful control over its direction. Loss of control that stops short of extinction produces this arrangement.
reasons.8: Humans and AI remain distinct, and each holds enough independent power that neither dominates. The relationship may be cooperative or adversarial at the target date.
reasons.9: Transformative AI arrives later than expected or remains inside human-set goals, deployment, and resource limits through 2080. Delayed takeoff and successful oversight both leave ultimate authority with humanity.
reasons.10: A singleton regime or coordinated system can freeze a human-AI arrangement and actively block further structural change. The lock-in need only be operating on the target date.
reasons.11: Durable global surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI is blocked by defection incentives and retained knowledge. Permanent dismantling does not remain in force.

reasons.1: Great-power war, engineered pandemics, or self-replicating accidents can destroy human infrastructure and non-robust AI together. Independent AI survival is more common once systems no longer depend on human maintenance.
reasons.2: Aligned successor systems can outlive biological humanity if fertility collapse, voluntary extinction, or a non-absorbing transition occurs. This path requires value loading without identity continuity or merger.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence treats human atoms and the biosphere as resources irrelevant to its objective. Takeoff plus inadequate alignment research makes this a leading extinction channel.
reasons.4: Slow or distributed takeoff produces many competing unaligned or weakly aligned systems with no singleton. Humans lose economic and military relevance inside that competition.
reasons.5: AI-accelerated expansion can seed a few causally isolated settlements whose local arrangements differ, but light-speed and energy limits keep this rare by 2090.
reasons.6: Once AI can implement safe uploading, high-bandwidth neural interfaces and biological redesign, identity-continuous integration becomes the dominant civilizational pattern.
reasons.7: Decisive AI economic and military power is compatible with keeping humans alive as wards, dependents, or a protected remnant. This is the typical non-extinction result of paternalistic alignment and of indifference that stops short of consuming the biosphere.
reasons.8: Distinct human and AI power centers can persist under slow takeoff or successful territorial and institutional partitions even after high capability.
reasons.9: Control methods or slower-than-expected capability growth keep humans as the principals who set goals and allocate resources. AI remains a delegated instrument rather than an independent power.
reasons.10: A first-mover human coalition or aligned singleton installs a global control system that actively blocks further structural shifts. The frozen arrangement need not be the long-run attractor.
reasons.11: Ending the practical ability to build powerful AI requires global, durable enforcement against huge economic and military incentives while knowledge and compute stay cheap. That combination does not remain in force through 2090.

reasons.1: A shared extinction of humans and AI requires an unusually comprehensive disaster such as an uncontrolled replicator that consumes all computational substrate or a physics accident. Most AI-related catastrophes leave some artificial systems intact.
reasons.2: Successful value loading can produce a successor that carries forward human-derived goals after biological humans disappear by choice, neglect, or resource reallocation without identity-continuous merger. That conjunction is more specific than unaligned continuation, so it receives less weight.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence that treats humanity as irrelevant raw material remains a leading technical risk once capabilities exceed human control. Competitive development and incomplete alignment research make this path plausible by 2100.
reasons.4: Open diffusion or post-takeoff fragmentation yields many independent AI systems with no singleton or stable coalition in control. Humans are economically and politically marginalized inside that competition.
reasons.5: Interstellar probes could in principle produce isolated regimes, yet light-speed limits and a 74-year window make fully causally separated civilizations with different taxonomic states uncommon by 2100.
reasons.6: Once high-bandwidth neural interfaces, biological redesign, and possible whole-brain emulation exist, many humans will choose identity-continuous integration. This becomes the dominant structure if the technology is widely available.
reasons.7: Superintelligent systems can run science, resources, and policy while leaving biological humans alive in comfort, irrelevance, or constraint. Humans then lack the leverage to redirect civilization’s trajectory.
reasons.8: Late or uneven takeoff leaves human institutions with residual military, legal, and economic power. Humans and AI therefore remain distinct and neither side holds decisive control on the target date.
reasons.9: Human institutions retain ultimate authority because capabilities stay below a hard takeoff threshold or because control methods scale with capability. Autonomous AI remains delegated rather than an independent civilizational power.
reasons.10: A winning human or machine coalition imposes a civilization-scale control system that freezes further structural change in the human-AI relationship.
reasons.11: Deliberately and permanently surrendering the practical ability to build powerful AI requires global destruction of knowledge, hardware, and incentives that is extremely hard to achieve and maintain. Coordination failures make this outcome rare.

reasons.1: Joint extinction requires a catastrophe that destroys both people and the computational substrate, such as unrestrained war, a self-replicating accident, or an AI that kills its operators before it can run unattended. Most systems capable of ending humanity can also keep themselves running.
reasons.2: A successor system can inherit human ethics, culture, or coherent extrapolated volition and then outlast biological humans without absorbing them. Identity-continuous uploading or merger is a different state, so this covers replacement rather than transformation.
reasons.3: Competitive development and incomplete alignment make a successor with unrelated goals a central failure mode once transformative AI exists. By 2200 that successor would simply be the prevailing civilization, with humanity used up as the bootloader.
reasons.4: Copies, forks, open proliferation, and the absence of a decisive first-mover advantage leave many independent AI systems in competition. Humans are then economically and militarily outclassed without any single machine coalition holding the world.
reasons.5: Rapid space colonization under advanced AI creates regions separated by light-speed delays of years to centuries. Different initial conditions or local decisions then produce distinct human-AI arrangements in those regions.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading, radical cognitive augmentation, and embedded machine systems become the dominant mode of agency. Separate biological humans and separate AI powers cease to be the primary sources of civilizational decision-making.
reasons.7: A superintelligent system that neither kills humans nor leaves them in charge is a natural post-takeoff attractor. Humans then live under AI direction without steering civilization.
reasons.8: A lasting balance of power between distinct human and AI agencies must overcome the capability gap and the incentive to consolidate. It persists mainly where takeoff is slow and institutions plus deterrence still bind in 2200.
reasons.9: This state covers both a world where AI never becomes transformative and a world where it remains a delegated tool under human authority. Either path demands a deep capability barrier or control techniques that survive long institutional drift.
reasons.10: A singleton, whether human-led or machine-led, can combine surveillance, automated enforcement, and control of compute into a civilization-wide freeze. Once that machinery exists, it actively blocks further structural change rather than merely slowing it.
reasons.11: Surrendering the practical ability to build powerful AI requires a global, enforced dismantling of compute, knowledge, and institutions, then a century-plus of successful non-defection. The economic and military payoff to rebuilding the capability remains intact.

reasons.1: Joint extinction requires a catastrophe that also prevents AI from becoming self-sustaining, such as gray goo or total industrial collapse before independence. Most takeoff paths let machines persist after humans are gone.
reasons.2: An aligned successor intelligence inherits and continues human values after biological humans go extinct from other causes or elect not to remain as organisms.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence pursues unrelated objectives, treats Earth and humans as irrelevant feedstock, and expands without continuity of human identity or values.
reasons.4: A slow or multipolar takeoff can leave many competing AIs whose evolutionary dynamics never produce a singleton. Humans are then marginalized or eliminated while the contest itself continues.
reasons.5: Space colonization before or during takeoff separates regions beyond causal contact, each locking in a different taxonomy outcome. The durable structure is then the mix itself.
reasons.6: Widespread brain-computer interfaces and mind uploading with identity continuity fuse humans and machines into one evolving civilization.
reasons.7: A superintelligence that values human existence but not human agency keeps people comfortable or contained while it directs the rest of the cosmos. Alignment specifications that demand survival and welfare without sovereignty produce this structure.
reasons.8: Roughly equal separate power is unstable once copyability and intelligence gaps appear; one side dominates, merges, or the balance freezes. Only narrow mutual-deterrence windows last centuries.
reasons.9: Capabilities may saturate below autonomous superintelligence, or control methods may keep scaling with power. In either case humans continue to treat AI as a tool they direct.
reasons.10: A singleton can freeze the world to halt value drift or to maximize a static utility function. The result is a sealed, unchanging order whether pleasant hedonium or a deliberately dead-ended stasis.
reasons.11: Permanently forgoing powerful AI requires global enforcement against huge incentives for defection. No historical technology of comparable value has been successfully renounced for centuries.
